title: Set Up a C Compiler and Development Environment
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and role of set up a c compiler and development environment in a C program.
Identify the relevant C language constructs, standard-library facilities or toolchain responsibilities.
Read a focused example and explain its data flow and control flow.
Recognize common errors, portability concerns and safety considerations for this topic.
Apply the concept in a small C program and verify it with compiler diagnostics and tests.

understand.concept: A C development environment combines a source editor, a compiler toolchain, a linker, a runtime environment and tools for testing and debugging. An editor stores source text; the compiler checks and translates it; the linker combines object code and libraries; the operating system runs the resulting program. These roles are related but are not interchangeable.
understand.whyItMatters: A reliable setup helps distinguish source-code mistakes from missing tools, incorrect build commands, linker failures and runtime problems. Knowing the build pipeline is essential when moving between a local computer, a classroom lab and a continuous-integration environment.
understand.analogy: Think of a C program as a set of precise instructions that must be translated for a particular machine and execution environment.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the formal C language rules, object lifetimes, types or implementation-defined behaviour.

explain.narrative:
Choose a compiler that supports the C standard you intend to learn. GCC and Clang are common open-source compiler families; Microsoft provides a C compiler in its Visual Studio toolchain. Installation and command names vary by operating system. After installation, verify the compiler version from a terminal rather than assuming the editor has configured it correctly.

A simple build typically has a compile-and-link step. For example, `cc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic main.c -o app` asks a C compiler driver to compile `main.c`, enable useful diagnostics and produce an executable named `app`. Run it using the platform's normal executable invocation. The exact command may differ on Windows or in managed environments.

Compiler warnings are valuable feedback. Fix warnings rather than hiding them. When a program has multiple source files, compile each translation unit and link them together. A build system becomes useful as the project grows. A browser-only playground cannot execute native C by itself; it needs a secure server-side compiler service or a local compiler environment.

examples.title: Check a compiler version
examples.explanation: The command reports which compiler driver is available and its version. If the command is not found, the compiler may not be installed or may not be on PATH.

examples.title: Compile with diagnostics
examples.explanation: This requests C17 mode and common warnings. The compiler driver also invokes the linker to create the executable.

practise.guidedTask: Install or open an approved C development environment. Verify the compiler version, create main.c with a minimal main function, compile with warnings enabled, run the program and save the exact build command.
practise.independentTask: Create a project folder with src and build directories. Compile a program from src into build, deliberately introduce one syntax error, one undeclared identifier and one linker error, then record how the diagnostics differ.
hints: A source editor is not a compiler.
A compiler warning may reveal a real defect even when an executable is produced.
The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries.
Use the same compiler and language standard consistently while learning.
Do not download unknown executables or paste untrusted code into an online compiler.
